tasks.description: Validation of core pagination functionality across the platform, focusing on state persistence during navigation, tab-specific pagination in the dashboard, and correct reset behavior during filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Navigate to the public browse page ('/browse?page=1'). Verify that the vehicle grid correctly displays the first 9 vehicles from the inventory.
On the '/browse' page, click the '2' button in the pagination footer. Verify that the URL updates to '/browse?page=2' and the second set of vehicles is rendered in the grid.
Navigate to the Manage Catalogue page at '/admin/catalogue?page=1'. Verify the vehicle table lists the first 10 records and the pagination highlights the first page.
On the Manage Catalogue page, click the 'Next' arrow button. Verify that the table updates to display the next set of 10 vehicle records.
On '/admin/catalogue?page=2', select 'Edit Vehicle' for any car. After saving the changes, verify that the application automatically redirects the user back to '/admin/catalogue?page=2'.
In the Admin Dashboard, switch to the 'Bookings' tab and navigate to page 2. Verify the URL includes 'bPage=2'. Switch back to the 'Vehicles' tab and verify its pagination state (vPage) is preserved.

On the Admin Dashboard (vPage=2), click the 'Edit' button for a vehicle. On the Edit page, click 'Back to Dashboard'. Verify the user is returned to the dashboard with the 'Vehicles' tab active and still on page 2.
On '/browse?page=2', enter a search term in the search bar. Verify that the application resets the results to Page 1 of the new search result set.
On the '/browse' page (Page 2), change the 'Condition' filter (e.g., from 'All' to 'New'). Verify that the pagination resets to Page 1 to display the filtered results.
Navigate to '/admin/catalogue?page=2' and perform a browser refresh. Verify the application stays on page 2 and persists the list state from the URL parameter.
Attempt to access the paginated Manage Catalogue ('/admin/catalogue?page=2') without a valid admin token. Verify the application blocks the request and redirects to the login page.
On the first page of any vehicle list (Catalogue or Browse), verify that the 'Previous' pagination button is disabled and does not allow navigation to a non-existent Page 0.
On the final page of the vehicle inventory in the Manage Catalogue, verify that the 'Next' pagination button is disabled and clicking it has no effect.
Perform a search on the Browse page that yields no matches. Verify that the pagination component is hidden from the UI when there are zero results.
In the 'Bookings' tab of the Admin Dashboard, if the total number of bookings is less than or equal to the items per page (10), verify that the pagination controls are not displayed.
